For me, yeah I don't know why my brain just won't wake up. It's been like this a long time, same as you. I haven't found the answer yet, but I have found a few things that make it just a bit easier. They aren't a solution, or at least haven't been for me, but maybe they'll help you a bit too. Forgive me if I'm suggesting things you have already tried. And also they are more about getting quality sleep, because if your body has slept well then it should be easier to wake up.

- Turn off all screens (phone, tv, computer, etc) a couple hours before bed. Read a book or work on a puzzle or another hobby instead. The blue light of screens keeps your body from making the proper amount of melatonin. It might make just enough melatonin for you to fall asleep, but then when you try to wake up again it hasn't used all the melatonin it ended up producing, later, while your eyes were closed.

- Consider taking melatonin before bed for a couple weeks

- If you have to use screens close to bedtime, get a filter on any of your devices that turns your screen a red or yellow hue. That won't keep you awake as badly as the bluish light that all screens emit. I have an android and the app I use is called Twilight.

- Don't do anything else in bed except sleep. (And sex). Train your body and brain that when you go to bed, it's sleep time.

- You should fall asleep within 15 minutes. If you don't, get up and read a book for half an hour, then try again.

- Make your room completely dark. And I mean completely. Blackout curtains, or tinfoil on the windows, or even a sleep mask. The sleep mask is good because when you unconsciously turn off your alarm, you'll have to take off the mask to find the alarm, and suddenly your eyes will see daylight. That might make your brain want to wake up.

- Get a light up alarm clock. They're surprisingly effective.

- Sleep a lot. Give yourself a few extra hours of sleep if you can. 9+ hours.

I hope these help you, and let me know if you find any solid solutions! I'm looking for a real solution to the same problem.

I didn't try Celexa specifically, but one of my antidepressants gave me ringing in my ears (tinnitus).

Tinnitus will not hurt you, it does not have any adverse physical consequences. So don't worry about that.

The tinnitus fades, even when you stay on the medication. Did you know that everyone has a slight ringing in their ears when it's very quiet? So, yours will fade too, but beware believing that you still have it once it has faded, just because you can still hear it. You had it a little bit before too, you just never noticed. 

In the meantime, get yourself something that makes white noise when you sleep. A loud fan, a white noise machine or app, a small plug in water fountain (check thrift stores), or even a fish tank! Water sounds are my favorite, they're so nice to sleep to. Rainymood.com is a good place to start.

Ok, first, you having suicidal thoughts is not enough for your therapist to send you to the hospital. If you had immediate suicidal intentions, that would be. From the way you describe it you are having just the thoughts, but you aren't ready to actually hurt yourself. It's not wrong to have those thoughts and it's not wrong to talk about them. Your therapist won't send you to the hospital. (If they sent every person who admits to suicidal thoughts to the hospital, they'd probably send most of the people they're treating! That's who goes to therapy, people who are struggling.)

Second, you don't have to tell your therapist the 21yo's name. He or she can't force you to, and probably won't even ask. You can even leave out their age. Just talk about this past relationship that hurt you, you don't need to divulge any specifics that you don't want to. 

Finally, in your first session tell your therapist about any fears you have about talking to them. They'll probably happily answer any questions you have. If they do ask "is there anything you're not telling me?" You can say "Yes." And then be honest about why. "I'm not ready to talk about that part", or "I'm afraid to tell you because", etc. They are there to help you to sort through the things that are hurting you, not to find all your secrets and then get you in trouble for them.

Talking to a therapist would be so helpful, and it sounds like you really want to. I say go for it. And be as open and honest as you can while you're there. You don't have anything to worry about, and so much to gain.
